newsitem.title: FINLAND: CULTOR SEES BIGGEST PROFIT IN 3RD TERTIAL.
newsitem.headline: CULTOR SEES BIGGEST PROFIT IN 3RD TERTIAL.

text.p: Finnish foodstuffs, animal feed and bakery group Cultor Oy's CEO Bjorn Mattson said on Wednesday the company now expected to generate most of full-year profit in the last tertial against the second tertial early this decade.
"The results get better in the third tertial and this means that the whole cyclicality of the company has changed," Mattson told a news conference on Cultor's January-April results.
"We have a lot businesses where the development in the beginning of the year is low and the autumn is stronger," he said.

The change was due partly to the greater emphasis of feeds unit Ewos in Cultor's nutrition business group, which was growing by more than 10 percent per year. The bulk of Ewos' net sales would come in the second half of the year, Mattson said.

Already last year, Cultor's net sales were strongest in the final tertial (September-December), Mattsson said, adding 1996 net sales had been low in the first tertial, stronger in the second and higher still in the final tertial.
That trend had been "even clearer" in operating profit, he said.
Cultor 1996 net sales and operating profit by tertial:
In the beginnig of the 1990s, Cultor's net sales had been lower early in the year, higher in the second tertial and again lower in the final tertial, Mattson said.

In January-April this year, Cultor's profit after financial items was 50 million markka, up two percent. It repeated a forecast of 1997 earnings at the 1995 level, when profit after financial items was 491 million markka and EPS 14.91 markka.
